_note: T2.5 test corpus. Two real cases of `version` declared in BOTH .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the marketplace entry. Observed on Claude Code 2.1.220. In both cases plugin.json's value is what lands in installed_plugins.json, confirming docs/02-architecture.md 3.3's 'plugin.json wins silently'. The DIVERGENT case is the positive test; the AGREEING case is the false-positive guard.

positive_divergent._why: Highest-value artifact. Both declarations live in the SAME upstream repo, in the SAME directory (.claude-plugin/), and disagree by three minor versions. This is upstream authoring drift, not a cache artifact: the marketplace entry was never bumped alongside plugin.json. A consumer reading the marketplace entry sees 2.2.1; the plugin actually installed is 2.5.0.

marketplace_metadata_version._note: marketplace.json ALSO carries a top-level metadata.version, which agrees with the stale entry, not with plugin.json. A third version-bearing field 3.3 does not mention.

sibling_skill_json._note: agrees with plugin.json; a 4th version-bearing file in the same repo.

negative_agreeing._why: False-positive guard. Double-declared but consistent. T2.5 must NOT flag this, or every well-maintained plugin trips the diagnostic.

detection_rule_implied: Flag when marketplaceEntry.version != null AND pluginJson.version != null AND the two strings differ. Report pluginJson.version as effective and marketplaceEntry.version as masked. Where they are equal, record the double declaration at INFO at most. Note that marketplace.json's top-level metadata.version is a THIRD field and tracked the stale entry here — decide explicitly whether T2.5 reads it.
